title: tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py BLOCKER: 14 table names duplicated between public and tenant_default (post ISS-0101/GH-359 cold-start full-suite run)
affected_areas: migrations (multiple non-GBL, non-scope-headered files creating tables now duplicated in public and tenant_default)
notes:
Discovered incidentally while resolving ISS-0101 (GH-359, shadow tenant_default.tenant/tenant_hostnames). Not the same defect and NOT caused by ISS-0101's fix (migrations/GBL-140_iss0101_drop_shadow_tenant_tables.sql, migrations/031_adp04b_tenant_realm_binding.sql, migrations/050_tenant_hostnames.sql, tools/clean_test_db.py) -- confirmed by running `python3 tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py` BEFORE any ISS-0101 changes were applied (6 duplicates: api_token_audit, event_payload_store, instance_definition_snapshots, lua_script_execution_audit, tenant_artifact_activations, variable_schemas -- `tenant`/`tenant_hostnames` were NOT in that list, they were separately allow-listed pending this exact fix) and AFTER a full cold-start `zig build test-integration` run plus `tools/clean_test_db.py` orphan sweep (14 duplicates: the original 6 plus group_roles, instance_waits, role_permissions, sessions, sla_records, subprocess_links, user_groups, webhook_deliveries). The growth from 6 to 14 across a single full-suite run indicates more source migrations lack the `-- scope: public` header + public.-qualification pattern GBL-134..140 established, so their unqualified CREATE TABLE reruns in the tenant_default pass on every fresh/cold provision the same way 031/050 did before this fix.

This is the same class of defect as ISS-0185/GH-518 (45 tables originally), ISS-0620/GH-573, ISS-0623/GH-580, ISS-0183/GH-516, and the still-open GH-482 (test-integration-svc 63 failing blocks, missing tenant_<uuid>.schema_migrations ledger) and GH-605/ISS-0630 (9 scope:public migrations breaking fresh-DB bootstrap) -- an ongoing, multi-issue lineage of dual-schema shadow tables from migrations written before the `-- scope: public` / public.-qualification convention (GBL-134 onward) was established. `docs/issue-reports/ISS-0185-diagnosis.yaml`'s classification_table does not cover these 8 newly-observed names (group_roles, instance_waits, role_permissions, sessions, sla_records, subprocess_links, user_groups, webhook_deliveries), so each needs the same GLOBAL_REGISTRY vs PER_TENANT classification work ISS-0185 did for its original 45 before a GBL-134/135-style corrective migration (or a source-migration scope-header patch, per the ISS-0101/GBL-140 precedent) can be written.

Out of scope for ISS-0101/GH-359: ISS-0101's acceptance criteria is specifically about `tenant`/`tenant_hostnames`, both confirmed removed from tenant_default and confirmed absent from this linter's duplicate list after the fix. This is a distinct, broader, pre-existing issue filed per CLAUDE.md's No-Issue-Left-Local-Only directive rather than folded into ISS-0101's fix.
candidate_resolution: For each of the 14 (or more, if the set grows further) duplicated table names: (1) classify as GLOBAL_REGISTRY (canonical=public) or PER_TENANT (canonical=tenant_default) per the ISS-0185 methodology (pg_constraint/pg_depend FK-chain analysis); (2) for GLOBAL_REGISTRY tables, either add a GBL-14x corrective DROP migration following the GBL-134/136/139/140 pattern AND patch the source migration with `-- scope: public` + public.-qualified DDL (the permanent fix, per ISS-0101/GBL-140 precedent -- prevents recurrence, not just a one-time cleanup); (3) for PER_TENANT tables, follow GBL-135's pattern (drop the public shadow). Given this keeps recurring (6 -> 14 tables observed growing within this session alone), consider a structural fix: a CI/pre-commit lint (extending tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py or tools/lint_migration_schema.py) that flags any NEW non-GBL migration file with an unqualified CREATE TABLE and no `-- scope: public`/`-- scope: all_schemas` header BEFORE it merges, rather than discovering the drift after the fact via a state-based linter run against an already-migrated database.
